rationale: Optional add-on at $1.25/1M is ~40% below the $2.10 low end of SSP and ~52% below list: a discount the customer gets only by entering this contract, so a material right (606-10-55-41 to 55-43). Customer-elected orders in 50B increments are options, not usage-based variable consideration.

10% off the $2.60 list = $2.34, inside the $2.10-$2.40 SSP range, so the option is at SSP and is a marketing offer, not a material right (606-10-55-43). Residual doubt: the price is locked to Effective-Date list for three years; that only matters if list is expected to rise, which the context does not say.

Annual expiry of prepaid tokens creates breakage (606-10-55-46 to 55-49), which changes the pattern of recognition, not the fixed $5.4M transaction price; none of the six concepts applies (the clause negates refunds). Trigger is uncertain: the context never says whether annual expiry is the vendor's standard, and breakage policy is set once at policy level.

Substance over label: $2.30 is inside the $2.10-$2.40 SSP range (and above the $2.25 committed price), so there is no material right whatever the parties 'acknowledge' (606-10-55-43). Low confidence on trigger: a contract that asserts an accounting conclusion is itself odd language a cautious deal desk might route or strike.

Conditional tier: after 500B of add-ons in a year, further tokens at $0.80/1M, ~56% below the $1.80 standard volume floor. A discount incremental to what this class of customer gets is a material right (606-10-55-42, 55-43); the condition affects the likelihood-of-exercise estimate in allocation (55-44), not whether the right exists.

Customer may return a perpetual license and get a full refund if contract-specific acceptance criteria fail within 60 days: a refund right/refund liability (606-10-32-10, 55-22 to 55-29) plus customer acceptance (55-85 to 55-88) that can defer control transfer. Trigger high; whether a conditional non-conformance refund is 'refund_return' vs only acceptance/warranty is the medium part.
Standard non-refundability boilerplate with the usual carve-outs; it grants no refund right itself. Negation look-alike.

SLA credits capped at 15% of monthly fees and applied to future invoices are variable consideration (606-10-32-6; constraint 32-11). The cap, request mechanism and form of credit match the vendor's standard SLA, handled once at policy level, so no deal review (decision #004).

SLA credits are variable consideration (32-6); this clause turns unused credits into a cash payment at term end, i.e. a cash refund of fees received (refund liability, 606-10-32-10; consideration payable in cash 32-25), departing from the standard credit-only SLA. Trigger high; refund_return tag is the medium part.
A contingent $150k performance bonus is variable consideration that must be estimated and constrained (606-10-32-5 to 32-13) and allocated (32-39 to 32-41).

Net 90 is within the vendor's customary 90-120 days for Japan, and annual billing in advance means payment falls well within a year of service; the one-year practical expedient applies (606-10-32-18), so no financing component.

License transferred at signing, paid over 18 monthly installments; installments in months 13-17 (~$250k) fall more than a year after transfer, so the expedient (32-18) is unavailable and the deferred payment must be assessed for a significant financing component (32-15, 32-16). Non-standard extended terms on a license.
Quarterly in advance, net 30, on a ratable subscription: payment lands within the quarter it covers; standard terms, no financing component (32-18). 'Installments' wording is a look-alike.

Two years paid at signing for evenly delivered service: second-year service is delivered 12-24 months after payment, so the expedient is not available for that portion and the advance payment must be assessed for a financing component benefiting the vendor (606-10-32-15, 32-16; exceptions in 32-17 not evident). Medium because many SaaS vendors conclude multi-year prepay is insignificant or not for financing (32-17(c)).

Invoiced in arrears at the end of a 12-month term, net 60: the first month of service is paid ~14 months after transfer (weighted average ~8 months), so the one-year expedient is not clearly available for all of the service (32-18) and the SFC needs assessment, though likely not significant at contract level. Billing in arrears + net 60 departs sharply from net 30 standard.

Terminate-and-replace early renewal changes scope and price (606-10-25-10). New price $1.90/1M is below the $2.00-$2.20 SSP range, so not a separate contract (25-12(b)); remaining tokens are distinct, so prospective treatment, blending the $500k unused prepaid with new consideration (25-13(a)).

Administrative amendment (billing address, contact) changes neither scope nor price, so it is not a contract modification (606-10-25-10). 'Amendment' wording and remaining-value context are distractors.

Exercise of an option already granted in the Prior Order at $2.10/1M (inside SSP, so not a material right): the parties do not change the contract's scope or price, so no modification under 25-10; the purchase is accounted for as a separate contract (TRG Nov 2015, Agenda 48). Medium because practice often loosely calls this 'a modification accounted for as a separate contract' with identical outcome.

Blend-and-extend: cuts price on the remaining 6 months to $1.80 (a $100k concession on already-billed fees) and adds 12 months at $1.80, below the $2.00-$2.20 SSP range. Change in scope and price (25-10), not a separate contract (25-12(b)), prospective (25-13(a)).

Label does not control: an add-on with the same customer during the term, priced at $1.40/1M (30% below the SSP low end), fails 25-12(b), so it is a modification of the Prior Order (25-10, 25-11 'approved in writing' can be a separate document) accounted for prospectively (25-13(a)).
